instructions: Rinse 1 1/2 cups of jasmine rice under cold water until it runs mostly clear. Transfer it to a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups of water and bring it to a boil. Cover, turn the heat to the lowest setting and cook for 12 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on until you serve.
Meanwhile, cut the chicken into bite size pieces and pat them dry. Sprinkle the 1/2 tsp salt over them.
Slice the onion. Seed the bell pepper and cut it into thin strips. Mince the garlic and grate 1 tsp of the ginger.
Juice one of the limes. Cut the other into wedges. Roughly chop 1/3 cup of the peanuts and the leaves from half the cilantro.
In a bowl, whisk 1/3 cup peanut butter with about 1/2 cup of the coconut milk until smooth. Whisk in the rest of the can, 2 tbsp soy sauce and 2 tsp brown sugar.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium high heat until it shimmers. Add half the chicken in a single layer and leave it alone for 3 minutes, until the underside is golden brown and lets go of the pan.
Turn the pieces and brown the other side for 2 minutes. Transfer them to a plate. They won't be cooked through yet.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil and brown the rest of the chicken the same way.
Turn the heat down to medium. Add the onion and bell pepper and cook, stirring and scraping up the browned bits, for 4 to 5 minutes, until they're soft and browned at the edges.
Add the garlic, ginger, 1/2 tsp coriander and 1/2 tsp cumin. Stir for about 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant.
Pour in the peanut sauce and bring it to a gentle bubble. Return the chicken and its juices to the pan.

Simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce coats a spoon. You're cooking the chicken to 175°F, so if you have a thermometer, check the thickest piece. No thermometer? Cut one open. It's done when there's no pink left.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the lime juice and the chopped cilantro.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of one of the lime wedges.
Serve over the rice with the peanuts on top, the lime wedges and the chili garlic sauce on the side.
method_notes: No version read had 20 or more ratings (Dinner at the Zoo, Feel Good Foodie, Half Baked Harvest, Budget Bytes and The Recipe Critic all blocked the reader) and RecipeTin Eats, the trusted cook for Thai, has no version of this dish, so the first read version leads. Seasons and Suppers simmers chicken thighs in coconut milk with peanut butter, soy, coriander, cumin and ginger and finishes with lime; The Foodie's Kitchen browns the chicken first and adds red pepper, garlic, fish sauce and honey; the SideChef version makes the sauce separately and tosses it with seared chicken. This one browns the thighs like The Foodie's Kitchen, uses more peanut butter than the lead so it tastes clearly of peanut, and keeps the chili garlic sauce at the table so the pan stays mild.
